# MCP conformance matrix

<!-- Generated by `node test/mcp-conformance/run.ts render-matrix` from requirements-2026-07-28.json, requirement-tests.json and requirement-matrix.md. Do not edit: `check-matrix` fails when this file is not current. -->

How VS Code conforms to the [MCP 2026-07-28 specification](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28): every normative sentence of the specification with the tests and the conformance scenarios that cover it, the results of the official conformance suite (`@modelcontextprotocol/conformance@0.2.0-alpha.12`) per scenario, and the deliberate deviations. VS Code is measured in two roles: as an MCP **client** (the workbench protocol engine, the extension-host transports and the OAuth client) and as an MCP **server** (the MCP gateway that serves VS Code's MCP servers to Copilot CLI over HTTP and gRPC).

The requirements are the 733 sentences of `docs/spec/requirements.zon` of [ChristianPresley/zig-sdk](https://github.com/ChristianPresley/zig-sdk) v0.5.2 (Apache-2.0), quoted from the specification at commit `046fa30efd374370afb87ef830bd788eac5f217e`. A requirement's party says who it binds: the client, the server, both, or an authorization server.

## Deliberate deviations

- **The 3 s resource read-cache floor.** The MCP resource file system coalesces reads of one resource for 3 seconds (`MOMENTARY_CACHE_DURATION` in `mcpResourceFilesystem.ts`), whatever `ttlMs` the server sent, also for `ttlMs: 0` or an absent hint, which the specification asks to treat as immediately stale. The floor keeps the editor, the file watcher and the chat attachments that read one resource at the same moment from issuing a request each. Results of input rounds are never cached. The caching rows `server/utilities/caching#011-98d047` and `#014-13ee1f` carry the deviation.
- **Tool names: the specification and the suite disagree.** The specification says tool names SHOULD be 1 to 128 characters of `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]` (`server/tools#017-c37d16`, `#019-49087d`). The suite's `tools-name-format` check (part of `completion-complete`) fails a server whose tool names are not 1 to 64 characters of `[A-Za-z0-9_./-]`: stricter on the length, looser on `/`. The gateway serves the names of the servers behind it unchanged, so a name of 65 to 128 characters passes the specification and fails the suite. The conformance fixture uses names that satisfy both.

## Supported JSON Schema dialects

VS Code validates schemas with its own validator (`src/vs/base/common/jsonSchemaValidator`):

| Dialect | `$schema` | Support |
| --- | --- | --- |
| JSON Schema 2020-12 (the default) | absent, or `https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema` (with or without `#`) | The required tests of the official JSON Schema Test Suite pass, except the groups of its skip list (`jsonSchemaTestSuite.test.ts`); `format` is an annotation. |
| JSON Schema draft-07 | `http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema` or its `https` form (with or without `#`) | The required draft-07 tests pass, except the groups of the skip list; `$ref` siblings are ignored, as draft-07 says. |
| Any other dialect | anything else | Rejected with an error that names the dialect. |

A `$ref` to a network URI is never fetched: it is a compile error. Validation is bounded in depth, subschemas, reference hops, evaluation steps and time.

## The typed gRPC binding

A gRPC server is reached through one of two bindings (`binding` in `mcp.json`). `auto`, the default, is the tunnel, exactly as `tunnel`: MCP requires a custom transport to keep the JSON-RPC message format, so VS Code never switches to the typed service on its own and speaks it only with `binding: "typed"`. A gRPC server that answers the tunnel's `server/discover` with a bare `UNIMPLEMENTED` fails to start with an error that names `"binding": "typed"` (this supersedes decision 11 of the plan, a tunnel-first probe with a typed fallback). The tunnel carries every JSON-RPC message; the typed service of the reference proto carries less:

| Feature | Tunnel (`mcp.zig.transport.v1.Mcp`) | Typed (`model_context_protocol.Mcp`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Requests and results of every method | yes (JSON-RPC messages in `JsonRpcMessage.jsonrpc`) | the eight RPCs of `model_context_protocol.Mcp`: `server/discover` (synthesized: it carries the `serverInfo` and `instructions` of the first typed ListTools response, else names the server after its authority), `tools/list`, `tools/call`, `resources/list`, `resources/templates/list`, `resources/read`, `prompts/list`, `prompts/get`, `completion/complete` |
| `subscriptions/listen` | yes (a server-streaming call) | no: answered with -32601 without a call |
| List-changed notifications | yes, on the listen stream | no (no listen stream) |
| `notifications/resources/updated` | yes, on the listen stream | no (no listen stream) |
| Pagination | yes | the first page only: a non-empty cursor is unexpressible |
| Progress and log notifications of a request | yes, streamed before the response | no |
| `structuredContent` that is not a JSON object | yes | no: unexpressible |
| Tasks extension (`resultType: "task"`, `tasks/*`) | yes | no: a result of the type task is unexpressible |
| Input rounds (`input_required`, `requestState`) | yes | yes (elicitation, sampling with one content block per message, roots) |
| Errors | `mcp-error-bin` trailer (the JSON-RPC error), else `mcp-error-code`, else the gRPC status | the same trailers; a JSON-RPC error ends the call with headers only |
| Lossy values | none | `destructiveHint: false` and `openWorldHint: false` arrive absent, an empty `blob` arrives as an empty `text`, `priority` keeps a 32-bit float |

## The gateway gRPC listener: `grpc_server.zig` parity

How the gateway gRPC listener checks a call, step by step, next to zig-sdk's `src/grpc/transport/grpc_server.zig` (`handleStreamInner`), the gRPC server of the reference implementation. A call that fails a step gets that step's answer and goes no further. [gateway-threats.md](../gateway-threats.md) maps the threat model of zig-sdk to the gateway's tests.

| Step | `grpc_server.zig` | Gateway | Tests |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Header list size | a header block over the limit: `ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM` (HTTP/2 layer) | a header list over 8 KiB: the stream is reset with `ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM` before anything else (Node applies `SETTINGS_MAX_HEADER_LIST_SIZE` only after the settings acknowledgement) | `grpcServer.test.ts` a header list over 8 KiB is reset with ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM |
| 1. `:method` | not `POST`: HTTP 405 | the same (with `allow: POST`) | `grpcServer.test.ts` a request that is not a POST gets HTTP 405, one without a gRPC content type 415 |
| 2. `content-type` | not `application/grpc…` (case-insensitive prefix): HTTP 415 | the same | `grpcServer.test.ts` a request that is not a POST gets HTTP 405, one without a gRPC content type 415 |
| 3. `:path` | neither the tunnel method nor a typed RPC: trailers-only `UNIMPLEMENTED` | the same, with `grpc-accept-encoding: identity` | `grpcServer.test.ts` an unknown path and a compressed encoding are UNIMPLEMENTED |
| 4. `grpc-encoding` | not `identity`: trailers-only `UNIMPLEMENTED` | the same, with `grpc-accept-encoding: identity` | `grpcServer.test.ts` an unknown path and a compressed encoding are UNIMPLEMENTED |
| 5. Authorization, before any look at the message | the bearer token of `authorization` (resource server): a challenge, else the principal | no authorization (loopback only): a `:authority` that is not a loopback name (`localhost`, an address of `127.0.0.0/8`, `[::1]`) is `PERMISSION_DENIED`; then the route (`mcp-gateway-route` metadata) is looked up, missing or unknown `NOT_FOUND`, trailers only, before the message is read; the route id is the principal of the sealed `requestState` | `grpcServer.test.ts` a refused :authority is PERMISSION_DENIED before the message is read<br>`mcpGatewayGrpc.test.ts` a foreign :authority is PERMISSION_DENIED<br>`mcpGatewayGrpc.test.ts` by default a call must name its route, even when the listener serves one: missing or unknown is NOT_FOUND, trailers only, before the message is read<br>`mcpGatewayGrpc.test.ts` input rounds: the sealed requestState continues on its own route only |
| `grpc-timeout` | parsed without overflow (`99999999H`) | malformed: `INVALID_ARGUMENT`; beyond what a timer can wait: no deadline; else the deadline cancels the dispatcher request and ends the call with `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED` | `grpcServer.test.ts` a grpc-timeout beyond what a timer can wait arms no deadline (3000000S, 99999999H)<br>`mcpGatewayGrpc.test.ts` a client reset and grpc-timeout cancel the request in the dispatcher |
| 6. The message | typed RPC: the typed handler; tunnel: the message, with nesting and size limits | over 4 MiB: `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED`; a missing, second or truncated message: `INVALID_ARGUMENT`; then the typed or the tunnel handler | `mcpGatewayGrpc.test.ts` a request message over 4 MiB is RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED<br>`grpcServer.test.ts` a missing, second, or truncated request message is INVALID_ARGUMENT |
| 7. Mirrored request metadata | `mcp-protocol-version`, `mcp-method`, `mcp-name` and `mcp-param-*` checked against the message: -32020 | the same checks as the HTTP route (`prepareModernRequest`): -32020 or -32022 in `mcp-error-bin`, before the request runs | `mcpGatewayGrpc.test.ts` a header mismatch ends the call before the request runs: -32020 in mcp-error-bin<br>`mcpGatewayGrpc.test.ts` typed metadata that disagrees with the message is -32020, an unsupported version -32022 |

### Authorization-server leg

The suite's `authorization` command tests an authorization server. It is not run.

| Scenario | Status | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `authorization-server-metadata-endpoint` | n/a | VS Code is an OAuth client and resource-server host, not an authorization server; the requirement sets have no authorization-server section. |
| `authorization-code-grant` | n/a | VS Code is an OAuth client and resource-server host, not an authorization server; the requirement sets have no authorization-server section. |

## Requirements

One table per page of the specification. Test citations name the file under `src/` or `test/` and the test; scenario citations name the leg, the revision and the scenario (and a check of it).

The rule covers the authorization server itself and its authorization and token endpoints at discovery, before anything is sent there, and the registration endpoint where a client registers: the OAuth client before its dynamic registration (with a configured prompt it asks for client credentials instead, as the product's providers do), and the product's dynamic authentication provider before it registers, at creation (by the creating server's escape hatch) or after invalid_client (by the escape hatch of the server whose request it serves: a provider is shared by the servers and the agent host that use the same authorization server and resource, and the workbench passes each server's rules with its requests); a pre-registered or Client ID Metadata Document client never contacts it, so a plain-HTTP registration endpoint does not fail discovery. The device authorization endpoint follows the same rule where the product's device code flow uses it, before its first request. The agent host's MCP sign-in creates its providers only from metadata whose issuer is the authorization server and whose authorization server, authorization, token and device authorization endpoints follow the rule (without an escape hatch). The enterprise-managed (XAA) sign-in applies the same rule, escape hatch included, to the resource authorization server it fetches metadata from and to the token endpoint that metadata names, before the IdP sign-in. |

backtracking is bounded: a pattern is not asserted, or only on strings it can test within the step budget<br>`jsonSchemaValidator.test.ts` a pattern that compiles only without the u flag is costed as that mode reads it: \u{N} repeats u, and a quantifier after an astral character repeats its trail surrogate<br>`jsonSchemaValidator.test.ts` long counts, lookaheads in loops and long sequences are costed: such a pattern is tested only on strings it can check within the step budget<br>`jsonSchemaValidator.test.ts` a repeated group with alternatives, or of varying length, is not asserted: a single RegExp.test cannot be interrupted<br>`jsonSchemaValidator.test.ts` patterns that need the ECMA-262 identity escapes of non-unicode mode compile and assert<br>`jsonSchemaValidator.test.ts` a pattern that compiles in neither mode is not asserted and the rest of the schema still validates<br>`mcpProtocolMeta.test.ts` an output schema with a pattern that cannot be compiled still checks the rest<br>`jsonSchemaValidator.test.ts` is detected from $schema and supports tuple items with additionalItems<br>`jsonSchemaValidator.test.ts` ignores 2020-12 keywords<br>`mcpService.test.ts` structured content that does not match the output schema rejects the tool call<br>`mcpProtocolMeta.test.ts` rejects content that does not match the schema<br>*Reason:* Schemas are validated in their declared or default dialect, except one keyword: a pattern (or patternProperties key) that the backtracking guard rejects (back-references, lookbehind, groups nested more than 64 deep, and repetitions it cannot prove linear: a repeated group with alternatives or of unbounded length, including nested unbounded quantifiers, and a group of varying length repeated without bound or so often that it can split a match in more than 256 ways), or that is not a regular expression with or without the u flag, is not asserted, and the schema's other keywords still are. Every other pattern gets a bound on the steps of one test, a polynomial in the input length for a backtracking matcher without V8's optimizations, read in the mode the pattern compiled in (without the u flag \u{3} is u three times): each character, class or assertion it examines is a step, a loop of 32 or more iterations (also a fixed count such as .{99999}) scans the input, a give-back that the rest of the pattern can start matching runs it again, a lookahead scans at every arrival, and an unanchored search runs at every position. A pattern whose bound exceeds 10 million steps already for strings of 64 characters (e.g. ^a*a*a*a*$ or \d+\d+\d+$, the fourth power of the input length) is not asserted; one whose bound grows faster than linearly or by more than 256 steps per character (e.g. ^[^@]+@[^@]+\.[^@]+$, an unanchored a+b, ^a*.{4000}!, or a 4000-character sequence tried at every position) is asserted only on strings whose bound stays within 10 million steps (2234, 2235, 3160 and 2497 characters); nothing is asserted about longer ones. The client logs a warning instead of refusing the whole schema, which would drop the tool (basic#046 asks for such bounds, and a time budget cannot interrupt a single regular expression match; patterns that need the non-unicode mode, such as \- or \#, compile and are asserted). |

The cited tests show allowed icons kept, icons with a type outside the allow list (SVG, BMP, text/html, none) dropped, also behind an allowed declared type, and a disallowed scheme dropped; no test feeds bytes that do not match every stated type (a remote file is not fetched before rendering). |
| [`#079-0fb934`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic#icons) | both | MUST | tested | Consumers of icon metadata MUST take appropriate security precautions when handling icons to prevent compromise: Maintain a strict allowlist of image types. | `mcpIcons.test.ts` includes supported icons and sorts sizes ascending<br>`mcpIcons.test.ts` drops icons whose MIME type is not on the allow list, declared or derived from the file name, SVG among them<br>*Note:* The allow list (WebP, PNG, JPEG, GIF) is a constant of mcpIcons.ts. |

both eras<br>`mcpGatewayDispatcher.test.ts` rate limits: a refusal by the route-wide bucket says that the server is busy, in the error and in the log, not that the client sent too many<br>`mcpGatewayDispatcher.test.ts` rate limits: generous defaults, false turns a limit off<br>`mcpGatewayRoute.test.ts` rate limits (service option): tools/call and completion/complete over the limit are -32603 rate_limited, per client, on both revisions<br>`mcpGatewayRoute.test.ts` rate limits: a client that changes its _meta client info, or opens a new 2025-11-25 session, at each call is held to the route-wide ceiling<br>`mcpGatewayGrpc.test.ts` a request over the route's rate limit ends with RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED on both bindings, -32603 rate_limited in mcp-error-bin<br>*Note:* Every gateway route rate-limits tools/call per client with a token bucket (default 50 a second, bursts of 100; IMcpGatewayServiceOptions.rateLimits configures or turns it off), on HTTP for both revisions and on gRPC. The specification names no error, so a call over the limit gets -32603 with data { reason: 'rate_limited', retryAfterMs, method, scope } (HTTP status 200; gRPC RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, the error in mcp-error-bin) and never reaches the server. A client is a 2026-07-28 client's address and _meta client info, a 2025-11-25 session, or a gRPC client's address and client info, kept as a fixed-size hash; an idle client's bucket is forgotten after 10 minutes. Since a client names itself, a route-wide bucket of 4 times the rate holds all clients together, so changing the client info or opening new sessions gains nothing. scope says which bucket refused the call: 'client' (the message says that this client sends too many) or 'route' (the message, and the gateway log, say that the server is busy). |
